title: Memory subjects, surfaces, and committed records — dark

routes.label: Subject index
routes.goal: Choose an explicit Memory subject and inspect state, role, store revision, worker availability, and long identities.
routes.dataState: Active and retired subjects spanning representative, empty, stale, failed, ungenerated, and unavailable states.

routes.label: Ready subject surface
routes.goal: Read the ready resident surface and scan active, resolved, and retracted committed Memories without nested vertical scrolling.
routes.dataState: Ready generated Markdown surface with long content, unsafe Markdown, wide table/code, provenance refs, and three lifecycle states.

routes.label: Committed Memory detail
routes.goal: Audit immutable Memory body, candidate evidence, source refs, derivations, and revision history.
routes.dataState: Current active revision with bounded typed provenance and active/resolved/retracted immutable history.

routes.label: Ready-empty subject
routes.goal: Distinguish a valid ready-empty snapshot and an empty committed Memory list from failure.
routes.dataState: Ready snapshot with empty Markdown and no refs; successful current list with no records.

routes.label: Stale subject surface
routes.goal: Recognize that no snapshot is displayable while committed Memories remain readable.
routes.dataState: Stale availability without snapshot and one resolved committed Memory.

routes.label: Failed subject surface
routes.goal: See generation failure without displaying a failed or partial snapshot.
routes.dataState: Failed availability without snapshot and one retracted committed Memory.

routes.label: Subject endpoint error
routes.goal: Keep each read-only region explicit when subject, surface, and current Memory requests fail.
routes.dataState: Intentional HTTP 503 from all subject-scoped endpoints.
